title: Field feedback compilation — Enterprise Security FAQ v2 (2026 Q1)
linked_artifacts: Slack: #sales thread 1708535099 (single link to latest kit)
content:
Internal working doc (GTM). Do not forward to customers. Purpose: capture repeated prospect/customer questions from AE/SE calls and security questionnaires in 2026 Q1, plus requested clarifications to fold into (a) Security FAQ v2, (b) one-pagers, and (c) standardized RFP response library.

Owner: Markus Klein (SE). Source inputs: SE call notes, AE deal threads, CS renewal escalations, and a handful of security questionnaire “free text” asks. Not exhaustive; it’s what came up repeatedly.

---

1) Executive summary (what’s causing friction)

Themes we see across late-stage deals:
- Customers struggle to understand the shared responsibility boundary across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. They ask the same question three times in different ways.
- “Audit logs” means different things to different teams (app-level logs vs admin/audit events vs inference request/response logs). Our answers sometimes sound like we log prompts/outputs by default (we should be precise).
- Data retention/residency questions are becoming the primary blocker in EMEA and regulated verticals.
- Incident notification wording is a flashpoint: customers push for hard timelines and broad definitions (“any incident anywhere”). Field needs safe, consistent language + a clear escalation path.
- SOC 2 scope and evidence sharing is fine operationally, but field wants a simple “how to get it” paragraph that doesn’t imply we can send the report to anyone.

Where this should land:
- FAQ v2: add 6–10 new Q&As, tighten wording on 8–12 existing ones.
- One-pagers: residency/retention and audit logging need “plain English” callouts; SSO/RBAC needs an “enterprise setup” snippet.
- RFP library: add variant answers (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) for the most common questionnaire prompts; add “when to route to Security/GRC/Legal.”

---

2) Who/where the feedback came from (high level)

North America (Stephanie Nguyen + team):
- Highest volume pushback on incident notification + pen test evidence + audit logging export to SIEM.

EMEA (Lukas Meyer + team):
- Residency as a blocker; customers ask for “EU-only processing” guarantees and very explicit statements on cross-border support access.

Solutions Engineering (Markus Klein / Simran Kaur):
- Lots of confusion on Dedicated vs Private; customers assume Dedicated = “single-tenant with customer-managed keys” by default.

Customer Success (Jasmine Liu / Liam O’Rourke):
- Renewals: requests for written confirmation of retention/deletion behavior; audit log sample events for GRC/SIEM teams.

---

3) Repeated questions & customer pushback (with suggested clarifications)

Format:
- What they ask (verbatim-ish)
- Why it’s confusing / what they actually mean
- Requested change to FAQ/RFP language
- Notes / routing

3.1 Data residency (biggest EMEA friction)

Q: “Can you guarantee data never leaves the EU (including metadata/logs/support access)?”
- Meaning: They want an explicit boundary: request payloads, outputs, logs/telemetry, and human access.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Add a residency section that separates:
    (a) customer content (prompts/outputs),
    (b) operational metadata (request IDs, timestamps, model name, token counts),
    (c) security/infra logs (admin/audit events),
    (d) support access.
  - Add “by deployment mode” matrix: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
  - Add a sentence on support access being controlled and logged; avoid implying “never accessed,” but clarify process and approvals.
- Notes/routing: For any “guarantee” requests, route to Security/GRC + Legal for contract language.

Q: “Is inference performed only in-region? Do you fail closed if a region is unavailable?”
- Meaning: They want to know if we spill traffic to another region under load/failover.
- Requested clarifications:
  - FAQ should state that routing/failover behavior is policy-driven and depends on product/deployment configuration; avoid absolute statements.
  - Add a “customer controls” line: what the customer can pin/choose (region selection) vs what Redwood may do operationally.
- Notes: Field wants an approved one-liner to avoid making availability promises that conflict with actual routing/fallback behavior.

3.2 Data retention & deletion

Q: “Do you store prompts and completions? For how long? Can we set it to zero?”
- Meaning: They’re mixing logging/telemetry with content storage.
- Requested clarifications:
  - FAQ needs a crisp statement distinguishing:
    - transient processing in memory,
    - customer content storage (if any),
    - logs/telemetry (what’s included/excluded),
    - customer-controlled retention settings (where supported).
  - Add explicit “what we do NOT do by default” language, but keep it accurate and scoped.
- Notes: This is often tied to HIPAA/PHI and financial data; SEs need a pointer to Private deployment boundary if customers require stronger guarantees.

Q: “If we delete data, does it also delete from backups? How quickly?”
- Meaning: They want deletion semantics and timelines.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Provide an approved answer pattern:
    - what can be deleted upon request / via controls,
    - backups lifecycle handled per internal policies,
    - avoid committing to a specific time window unless contractually agreed.
- Routing: If they push for exact timeframes, route to GRC.

3.3 Audit logging (terminology mismatch)

Q: “Do you have audit logs?” (followed by) “Can you send our SIEM all user actions and API calls?”
- Meaning: Customers want admin/audit events (auth changes, key changes, role changes) and sometimes also want API request logs.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Rename/clarify FAQ section heading to “Administrative audit logs” (or similar) and explicitly define scope.
  - Provide examples of event categories (login/SSO events, API key lifecycle, RBAC changes, org/project changes, policy changes) without over-listing every event name.
  - Add SIEM/export language carefully: “export options” vs “we natively integrate with every SIEM.”
- Notes: Multiple customers asked for “sample events.” We should have a ready-to-share sanitized sample (or at least a snippet in the one-pager).

Q: “Do you log prompts/outputs in audit logs?”
- Meaning: They’re concerned about sensitive content being included in logs.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Add a direct Q&A: “Are prompts and outputs included in administrative audit logs?” with a straightforward answer and the usual caveats (debugging, support workflows, customer configuration, deployment mode).
- Routing: If they ask for “no logging ever,” route to Security/GRC to avoid over-commitments.

3.4 Incident response & notification (highest sensitivity)

Q: “Will you notify us within 24/48/72 hours of any security incident?”
- Meaning: They want a firm clock and a broad definition.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Provide an approved paragraph that:
    - ties notification timing to contract terms,
    - defines the scope as “confirmed incident affecting customer data/systems” (avoid promising notification for all incidents everywhere),
    - explains that investigation/containment precedes full details and that updates are iterative.
  - Add “how customers get updates” (status page / named channels), but avoid promising a single mechanism if it varies.
- Notes: AEs asked for consistent definition of “security incident” vs “breach.” We should align FAQ wording with what Legal will accept in MSAs.

Q: “Do you have a public status page? Do you publish postmortems?”
- Meaning: Reliability + transparency expectations.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Add a simple FAQ entry: status communications are available; post-incident communications depend on severity/contract; avoid “we always publish postmortems.”

3.5 SSO/SAML, SCIM, and RBAC (setup clarity)

Q: “Do you support SAML SSO? Is it enforced for all users? Do you support SCIM?”
- Meaning: They want enterprise identity lifecycle management and enforcement.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Add a short “recommended enterprise setup” snippet:
    - enforce SSO,
    - restrict invites/domains,
    - least-privilege roles,
    - break-glass admin guidance.
  - If SCIM support varies by plan or is limited, document it clearly and avoid implying full SCIM if not universally available.
- Notes: Buyers also ask if service accounts can bypass SSO (API keys). We need one sentence explaining how API keys are managed and audited.

Q: “Can you do per-project RBAC? Can we restrict specific models?”
- Meaning: They want multi-team boundaries and control-plane scoping.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Add RFP variants: org-level vs project-level roles and how they apply across deployment modes.

3.6 Encryption & key management (KMS/HSM expectations)

Q: “Is data encrypted at rest/in transit? Can we bring our own keys (BYOK)?”
- Meaning: They’re asking about customer-managed keys and HSM-backed KMS.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Ensure the FAQ answers differentiate:
    - encryption in transit (TLS),
    - encryption at rest (platform-managed),
    - customer-managed keys options (where available; if only for Private or specific configurations, say so).
- Notes: Dedicated customers often assume they get BYOK “by default.” We should explicitly state what’s standard vs add-on / Private.

3.7 Dedicated vs Private deployment boundary (persistent confusion)

Q: “Is Dedicated the same as Private?” / “If we buy Dedicated, is it in our VPC?”
- Meaning: They’re mixing “single-tenant compute” with “customer network boundary.”
- Requested clarifications:
  - Add a plain-English comparison table:
    - Hosted: shared control plane + shared compute pools (multi-tenant)
    - Dedicated: dedicated compute capacity with isolation, but still operated by Redwood (and networking specifics clarified)
    - Private: customer-managed network boundary (VPC/on-prem) with clearer customer responsibilities
  - Add an explicit “who operates what” line for patching, monitoring, access controls, logging.
- Notes: This comes up most in regulated prospects (health/finance/public sector). SEs request a canonical diagram (even if simple).

3.8 Subprocessors & DPA requests

Q: “Send your subprocessors list + DPA + where data is processed.”
- Meaning: They want procurement-ready artifacts and a stable URL.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Provide a consistent answer pattern:
    - “We maintain a current subprocessor list; available upon request / at <canonical location>” (depending on policy)
    - DPA via Legal channel
  - Field request: one place to point customers to “latest security kit” (link hygiene problem).

3.9 Vulnerability management & pen testing evidence

Q: “When was your last pen test? Can we see the full report?”
- Meaning: They want assurance + artifacts.
- Requested clarifications:
  - Add FAQ language: we conduct regular third-party testing; sharing is controlled (NDA) and typically via executive summary / attestation or as approved.
  - Provide a “what we can share” checklist so AEs don’t improvise.
- Notes: Customers often accept a summary letter + remediation statement if delivered quickly.

---

4) Confusing wording / terms to fix (specific callouts)

4.1 “We do not store customer data” (too absolute)
- Field concern: Several FAQs/answers sound like “never stored” which triggers follow-ups on logs/backups.
- Proposal: Replace absolutes with scoped statements (what we store, what we don’t, and under what conditions).

4.2 “Audit logs” (needs definition upfront)
- Proposal: Start the audit log section with a definition and an explicit exclusion statement (e.g., not equivalent to full request/response logging).

4.3 “Private deployment” (customers assume full customer operation)
- Proposal: Add a sentence: “Private changes the network boundary and responsibility split; operational responsibilities are defined in the deployment runbook/contract.”

4.4 “Incident notification” (avoid timeline claims)
- Proposal: Keep a single blessed paragraph for all field use; anything else routes to GRC/Legal.

---

5) Requested assets (field asks for these repeatedly)

1) “Latest security kit” single link
- Problem: AEs are sharing stale PDFs. Prospects ask for “the latest” and we don’t have a canonical pointer.
- Requested: one Confluence canonical page + a Drive folder link for PDFs with controlled permissions.

2) Sanitized sample audit log events
- Requested by: multiple customers + SUP-19344.
- Target: 1-page appendix (or a snippet inside audit logging one-pager).

3) One-page Dedicated vs Private comparison (diagram)
- Requested by: regulated prospects; helps reduce cycles.

4) Residency/retention “plain English” callouts
- Requested by: EMEA AEs; the current narrative is too nuanced for procurement reviewers.

---

6) Proposed additions to FAQ v2 (new Q&As)

Suggested new questions to add (titles only; wording TBD by Security/GRC):
- “What customer content is included in logs and telemetry?”
- “Are prompts/outputs included in administrative audit logs?”
- “Can we export administrative audit logs to our SIEM?”
- “How do Hosted, Dedicated, and Private differ in security responsibilities?”
- “What are your data residency controls by deployment mode?”
- “What are your retention and deletion practices (and what can customers configure)?”
- “How does Redwood handle incident notification?”
- “How can we request SOC 2 report access and other compliance evidence?”
- “Do you support SSO enforcement and (if applicable) SCIM provisioning?”
- “What is Redwood’s approach to vulnerability management and penetration testing?”

---

7) Deal snippets (anonymized) illustrating the friction

Snippet A (Northbridge security review call):
- Prospect asked “audit logs” three times; they meant SIEM export of admin actions. We answered generically, then they followed up asking if prompts are logged. Recommendation: define audit logs + explicitly exclude prompts/outputs unless configured.

Snippet B (Omnihealth Private deep dive):
- Confusion between Dedicated and Private led to 2-week stall while they re-did their internal architecture review. Recommendation: add a “Dedicated vs Private” diagram and a shared responsibility table.

Snippet C (EMEA residency blocker):
- Legal/procurement asked for a guarantee that “no data leaves EU.” We didn’t have a clear “what we can promise” statement; deal pushed to Private evaluation. Recommendation: provide policy-driven language and escalation guidance.

---

8) Action items / owners (proposed)

- Naomi Feldman (Security PM): incorporate top themes into Security FAQ v2 + align with GRC/Legal review.
- Olga Petrov (GRC): approve evidence-sharing language + the “how to request SOC 2” paragraph.
- Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei (Security Eng): confirm audit log scope, provide sample event categories, and validate SIEM export wording.
- Elliot Price / Docs: ensure public-doc link hygiene and that any externally referenced page matches internal phrasing.
- Soojin Lee (PMM): propose one-pager template updates and a “single link” distribution plan for the field.

Open questions to resolve in review:
- What is the most accurate, least risky way to describe prompt/output retention in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
- What is the approved default stance on cross-region failover wording (residency vs availability)?
- What’s the exact boundary of “administrative audit logs” vs “request logs” in current product?

---

9) Notes to self / next update

- Next pass: convert this doc into a checklist mapped to FAQ sections + RFP library entries (so we can verify each field issue has a home).
- Add a short “if customer asks X, send Y” routing guide (FAQ PDF vs one-pager pack vs evidence request process).
- Once FAQ v2 is published in Confluence, update this doc with links to the exact Q&A anchors that changed.
